ECE 685 | Power Systems Design L34
Power Flow III
Power equations, bus types, and a solved case
Buxin She
Mike Wiegers Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

Lecture outline
1 Power equations: express real and reactive power in terms of bus voltages.
2 Bus types: count quantities and equations, then identify specified and unknown
variables.
3 Inductive lines: interpret power transfer and its power-angle maximum.
4 Worked example: identify knowns and unknowns, write equations, and interpret
a solution.

Summary
The power equations relate bus voltages to real and reactive injections.
Bus types identify specified quantities and the unknowns to be determined.
An inductive line relates real power to angle and reactive power to voltage
magnitude.
A power flow solution supplies the bus state; currents, branch flows, and losses
follow from it.
The example follows one route: system and operating data, knowns and unknowns,
power flow equations, then numerical results.
